sanskrit: jyeṣṭhāmūlaṃ tu yo māsam ekabhaktena saṃkṣapet aiśvaryam atulaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ pumān strī vābhijāyate
english: Whoever passes the month of Jyeṣṭhāmūla taking but a single meal each day—man or woman—is reborn to sovereignty unrivalled and supreme.

sanskrit: āṣāḍham ekabhaktena sthitvā māsam atandritaḥ bahudhānyo bahudhano bahuputraś ca jāyate
english: He who, unwearying, keeps the month of Āṣāḍha upon a single meal each day is born rich in grain, rich in wealth, and rich in sons.

sanskrit: śrāvaṇaṃ niyato māsam ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet yatra tatrābhiṣekeṇa yujyate jñātivardhanaḥ
english: He who, self-controlled, passes the month of Śrāvaṇa upon a single meal is everywhere joined to royal consecration, and the increaser of his kinsmen.

sanskrit: prauṣṭhapadaṃ tu yo māsam ekāhāro bhaven naraḥ dhanāḍhyaṃ sphītam acalam aiśvaryaṃ pratipadyate
english: The man who through the month of Prauṣṭhapada eats but once a day attains a lordship rich in wealth, flourishing, and unshakable.

sanskrit: tathaivāśvayujaṃ māsam ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet prajāvān vāhanāḍhyaś ca bahuputraś ca jāyate
english: Likewise he who passes the month of Āśvayuja upon a single meal is born blessed with offspring, rich in conveyances, and abounding in sons.

sanskrit: kārttikaṃ tu naro māsaṃ yaḥ kuryād ekabhojanam śūraś ca bahubhāryaś ca kīrtimāṃś caiva jāyate
english: The man who, through the month of Kārttika, takes but one meal a day is born a hero, with many wives, and crowned with renown.

sanskrit: iti māsā naravyāghra kṣapatāṃ parikīrtitāḥ tithīnāṃ niyamā ye tu śṛṇu tān api pārthiva
english: Thus, O tiger among men, have the months been proclaimed for those who fast through them. Now hear too, O king, the observances reckoned by the lunar days.

sanskrit: pakṣe pakṣe gate yas tu bhaktam aśnāti bhārata gavāḍhyo bahuputraś ca dīrghāyuś ca sa jāyate
english: He who eats a meal only when each fortnight has run its course, O Bhārata, is born rich in cattle, abounding in sons, and long of life.

sanskrit: māsi māsi trirātrāṇi kṛtvā varṣāṇi dvādaśa gaṇādhipatyaṃ prāpnoti niḥsapatnam anāvilam
english: He who, month by month for twelve years, fasts through three nights at a stretch attains lordship over hosts, free of rivals and unsullied.

sanskrit: ete tu niyamāḥ sarve kartavyāḥ śarado daśa dve cānye bharataśreṣṭha pravṛttim anuvartatā
english: All these observances, O best of the Bharatas, are to be performed for twelve autumns by one who keeps to the round of active life.

sanskrit: yas tu prātas tathā sāyaṃ bhuñjāno nāntarā pibet ahiṃsānirato nityaṃ juhvāno jātavedasam
english: But he who eats at dawn and again at evening, drinking nothing between, ever devoted to non-injury and pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhiḥ sa varṣair nṛpate sidhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ agniṣṭomasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: —that man, O king, is perfected in six years, of this there is no doubt, and gains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: adhivāse so 'psarasāṃ nṛtyagītavinādite taptakāñcanavarṇābhaṃ vimānam adhirohati
english: He mounts a celestial car bright as molten gold, in the dwelling of the apsarases that resounds with dance and song.

sanskrit: pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu brahmaloke mahīyate tatkṣayād iha cāgamya māhātmyaṃ pratipadyate
english: For a full thousand years he is honoured in the world of Brahmā, and when that is spent he returns here to attain greatness.

sanskrit: yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇam ekāhāro bhaven naraḥ atirātrasya yajñasya sa phalaṃ samupāśnute
english: The man who through a full year takes but a single meal a day enjoys the fruit of the Atirātra sacrifice.

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi svarge ca sa mahīyate tatkṣayād iha cāgamya māhātmyaṃ pratipadyate
english: For ten thousand years he is honoured in heaven, and when that is spent he returns here to attain greatness.

sanskrit: yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ caturthaṃ bhaktam aśnute ahiṃsānirato nityaṃ satyavāṅ niyatendriyaḥ
english: He who through a full year eats only every fourth mealtime, ever devoted to non-injury, truthful in speech, his senses curbed—

sanskrit: vājapeyasya yajñasya phalaṃ vai samupāśnute triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi svarge ca sa mahīyate
english: —he indeed enjoys the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice, and for thirty thousand years he is honoured in heaven.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhe kāle tu kaunteya naraḥ saṃvatsaraṃ kṣapet aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Should a man, O son of Kuntī, pass a whole year eating only at every sixth mealtime, he gains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: cakravākaprayuktena vimānena sa gacchati catvāriṃśat sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ divi modate
english: He travels in a celestial car yoked with cakravāka birds, and rejoices in heaven for forty thousand years.

sanskrit: aṣṭamena tu bhaktena jīvan saṃvatsaraṃ nṛpa gavāmayasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Living through a whole year, O king, upon only every eighth meal, a man gains the fruit of the Gavāmayana sacrifice.

sanskrit: haṃsasārasayuktena vimānena sa gacchati pañcāśataṃ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ divi modate
english: He travels in a celestial car yoked with swans and cranes, and rejoices in heaven for fifty thousand years.

sanskrit: pakṣe pakṣe gate rājan yo 'śnīyād varṣam eva tu ṣaṇmāsānaśanaṃ tasya bhagavān aṅgirābravīt ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇi divam āvasate ca saḥ
english: He who for a whole year, O king, eats only when each fortnight has passed—of his half-year of abstinence the venerable Aṅgiras has spoken—dwells in heaven for sixty thousand years.

sanskrit: vīṇānāṃ vallakīnāṃ ca veṇūnāṃ ca viśāṃ pate sughoṣair madhuraiḥ śabdaiḥ suptaḥ sa pratibodhyate
english: And there, O lord of peoples, as he sleeps he is roused by the sweet, well-tuned notes of vīṇās and lutes and flutes.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaram ihaikaṃ tu māsi māsi pibet payaḥ phalaṃ viśvajitas tāta prāpnoti sa naro nṛpa
english: And he who through one year here drinks milk only once a month—that man, dear child, O king, gains the fruit of the Viśvajit sacrifice.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghraprayuktena vimānena sa gacchati saptatiṃ ca sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ divi modate
english: He travels in a celestial car yoked with lions and tigers, and rejoices in heaven for seventy thousand years.

sanskrit: māsād ūrdhvaṃ naravyāghra nopavāso vidhīyate vidhiṃ tv anaśanasyāhuḥ pārtha dharmavido janāḥ
english: Beyond a month, O tiger among men, no fast is ordained; but the rule of utter abstinence from food, O Pārtha, those versed in dharma declare thus.

sanskrit: anārto vyādhirahito gacched anaśanaṃ tu yaḥ pade pade yajñaphalaṃ sa prāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ
english: He who, untroubled and free of disease, undertakes the fast unto death gains, at every step, the fruit of a sacrifice; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: divaṃ haṃsaprayuktena vimānena sa gacchati śataṃ cāpsarasaḥ kanyā ramayanty api taṃ naram
english: He goes to heaven in a celestial car yoked with swans, and a hundred apsaras-maidens delight that man.

sanskrit: ārto vā vyādhito vāpi gacched anaśanaṃ tu yaḥ śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ modate divi sa prabho kāñcīnūpuraśabdena suptaś caiva prabodhyate
english: And he who, even if afflicted or diseased, undertakes the fast unto death rejoices in heaven, O lord, for a hundred thousand years, and as he sleeps is roused by the sound of girdles and anklets.

sanskrit: sahasrahaṃsasaṃyukte vimāne somavarcasi sa gatvā strīśatākīrṇe ramate bharatarṣabha
english: Borne in a celestial car yoked with a thousand swans, gleaming like the moon and thronged with a hundred women, he goes and there takes his delight, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: kṣīṇasyāpyāyanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kṣatasya kṣatarohaṇam vyādhitasyauṣadhagrāmaḥ kruddhasya ca prasādanam
english: For the wasted, replenishment is seen as good; for the wounded, the healing of the wound; for the diseased, a wealth of medicines; and for the angry, appeasement.

sanskrit: duḥkhitasyārthamānābhyāṃ dravyāṇāṃ pratipādanam na caite svargakāmasya rocante sukhamedhasaḥ
english: For the suffering, the bestowal of goods through wealth and honour: yet none of these please the man who longs for heaven and would prosper in happiness.

sanskrit: ataḥ sa kāmasaṃyukto vimāne hemasaṃnibhe ramate strīśatākīrṇe puruṣo 'laṃkṛtaḥ śubhe
english: Therefore that man, his desires fulfilled and richly adorned, takes his delight in a fair celestial car bright as gold and thronged with a hundred women.

sanskrit: svasthaḥ saphalasaṃkalpaḥ sukhī vigatakalmaṣaḥ anaśnan deham utsṛjya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Serene, his resolve fulfilled, happy, and purged of every stain, the man who casts off his body by fasting gains this fruit.

sanskrit: bālasūryapratīkāśe vimāne hemavarcasi vaiḍūryamuktākhacite vīṇāmurajanādite
english: In a celestial car gleaming like gold, radiant as the newly risen sun, inlaid with beryl and pearls, resounding with vīṇā and drum,

sanskrit: patākādīpikākīrṇe divyaghaṇṭāninādite strīsahasrānucarite sa naraḥ sukham edhate
english: strewn with banners and lamps, ringing with celestial bells, attended by a thousand women—there that man thrives in bliss.

sanskrit: yāvanti romakūpāṇi tasya gātreṣu pāṇḍava tāvanty eva sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ divi modate
english: For as many thousands of years, O Pāṇḍava, as there are pores of hair upon his limbs, even so long does he rejoice in heaven.

sanskrit: nāsti vedāt paraṃ śāstraṃ nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ na dharmāt paramo lābhas tapo nānaśanāt param
english: There is no scripture higher than the Veda, no teacher like a mother; there is no gain greater than dharma, no austerity beyond fasting.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyaḥ paraṃ nāsti pāvanaṃ divi ceha ca upavāsais tathā tulyaṃ tapaḥkarma na vidyate
english: There is no purifier higher than the brāhmaṇas, in heaven or here below; and no act of austerity is known that is the equal of fasting.

sanskrit: upoṣya vidhivad devās tridivaṃ pratipedire ṛṣayaś ca parāṃ siddhim upavāsair avāpnuvan
english: By fasting in due form the gods attained the threefold heaven, and the seers won the highest perfection through fasts.

sanskrit: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ hi viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā kṣāntam ekena bhaktena tena vipratvam āgataḥ
english: For a thousand celestial years the wise Viśvāmitra endured upon but a single meal, and thereby came to brāhmaṇahood.

sanskrit: cyavano jamadagniś ca vasiṣṭho gautamo bhṛguḥ sarva eva divaṃ prāptāḥ kṣamāvanto maharṣayaḥ
english: Cyavana and Jamadagni, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, and Bhṛgu—all these great seers, steadfast in endurance, attained to heaven.

sanskrit: idam aṅgirasā pūrvaṃ maharṣibhyaḥ pradarśitam yaḥ pradarśayate nityaṃ na sa duḥkham avāpnute
english: This of old was made known by Aṅgiras to the great seers; he who ever makes it known meets with no sorrow.

sanskrit: imaṃ tu kaunteya yathākramaṃ vidhiṃ; pravartitaṃ hy aṅgirasā maharṣiṇā paṭheta yo vai śṛṇuyāc ca nityadā; na vidyate tasya narasya kilbiṣam
english: And this rule in due order, O son of Kuntī, set forth by the great seer Aṅgiras—whoever recites it or hearkens to it without fail, no sin is found in that man.

sanskrit: vimucyate cāpi sa sarvasaṃkarair; na cāsya doṣair abhibhūyate manaḥ viyonijānāṃ ca vijānate rutaṃ; dhruvāṃ ca kīrtiṃ labhate narottamaḥ
english: He is freed from every defilement, nor is his mind overborne by faults; he comes to understand the cries of creatures born of other wombs, and that best of men attains enduring renown.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmahena vidhivad yajñāḥ proktā mahātmanā guṇāś caiṣāṃ yathātattvaṃ pretya ceha ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The sacrifices have been duly declared by the great-souled grandsire, and their virtues set forth truly, in every respect, both in the next world and in this.

sanskrit: na te śakyā daridreṇa yajñāḥ prāptuṃ pitāmaha bahūpakaraṇā yajñā nānāsaṃbhāravistarāḥ
english: But those sacrifices cannot be attained by a poor man, O grandsire; sacrifices require many appurtenances and a vast array of varied materials.

sanskrit: pārthivai rājaputrair vā śakyāḥ prāptuṃ pitāmaha nārthanyūnair avaguṇair ekātmabhir asaṃhataiḥ
english: They can be undertaken by kings or by princes, O grandsire, but not by those wanting in wealth, lacking in means, solitary, and unsupported.

sanskrit: yo daridrair api vidhiḥ śakyaḥ prāptuṃ sadā bhavet tulyo yajñaphalair etais tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: That rule which even the poor might always be able to follow, and which would be equal to these fruits of sacrifice—tell me of it, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca idam aṅgirasā proktam upavāsaphalātmakam vidhiṃ yajñaphalais tulyaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: This was declared by Aṅgiras, a rule whose essence is the fruit of fasting and which is equal to the fruits of sacrifice; learn it now, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yas tu kalyaṃ tathā sāyaṃ bhuñjāno nāntarā pibet ahiṃsānirato nityaṃ juhvāno jātavedasam
english: He who eats at dawn and again at evening, drinking nothing between, ever devoted to non-injury and pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhir eva tu varṣaiḥ sa sidhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ taptakāñcanavarṇaṃ ca vimānaṃ labhate naraḥ
english: —that man is perfected in just six years, of this there is no doubt, and he gains a celestial car of the colour of molten gold.

sanskrit: devastrīṇām adhīvāse nṛtyagītaninādite prājāpatye vaset padmaṃ varṣāṇām agnisaṃnibhe
english: In the dwelling of the celestial women, resounding with dance and song, blazing like fire, he abides in the realm of Prajāpati for a padma of years.

sanskrit: trīṇi varṣāṇi yaḥ prāśet satataṃ tv ekabhojanam dharmapatnīrato nityam agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: He who for three years eats but a single meal continually, ever faithful to his wedded wife, gains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma.

sanskrit: dvitīye divase yas tu prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśamāsāṃs tu juhvāno jātavedasam yajñaṃ bahusuvarṇaṃ vā vāsavapriyam āharet
english: And he who, eating only on every second day a single meal for all twelve months while pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire, would thereby win the fruit of a Bahusuvarṇa sacrifice, dear to Vāsava—

sanskrit: satyavāg dānaśīlaś ca brahmaṇyaś cānasūyakaḥ kṣānto dānto jitakrodhaḥ sa gacchati parāṃ gatim
english: —truthful in speech, given to charity, devoted to brāhmaṇas, free of malice, patient, self-restrained, his anger conquered—that man attains the highest goal.

sanskrit: pāṇḍurābhrapratīkāśe vimāne haṃsalakṣaṇe dve samāpte tataḥ padme so 'psarobhir vaset saha
english: In a celestial car bright as a pale white cloud and marked with the sign of the swan, when two padmas are complete he dwells together with the apsarases.

sanskrit: tṛtīye divase yas tu prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśamāsāṃs tu juhvāno jātavedasam
english: And he who eats only on every third day a single meal, for all twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: atirātrasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam mayūrahaṃsasaṃyuktaṃ vimānaṃ labhate naraḥ
english: —that man gains the unsurpassed fruit of the Atirātra sacrifice, and obtains a celestial car yoked with peacocks and swans.

sanskrit: saptarṣīṇāṃ sadā loke so 'psarobhir vaset saha nivartanaṃ ca tatrāsya trīṇi padmāni vai viduḥ
english: In the world of the Seven Seers he dwells ever together with the apsarases, and his term there, they say, is three padmas before his return.

sanskrit: divase yaś caturthe tu prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśamāsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: And he who eats only on every fourth day a single meal, for all twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: vājapeyasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam indrakanyābhirūḍhaṃ ca vimānaṃ labhate naraḥ
english: —that man gains the unsurpassed fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice, and obtains a celestial car bestrode by the daughters of Indra.

sanskrit: sāgarasya ca paryante vāsavaṃ lokam āvaset devarājasya ca krīḍāṃ nityakālam avekṣate
english: At the very bounds of the ocean he dwells in the world of Vāsava, and for all time beholds the sport of the king of the gods.

sanskrit: divase pañcame yas tu prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśamāsāṃs tu juhvāno jātavedasam
english: And he who eats only on every fifth day a single meal, for all twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: alubdhaḥ satyavādī ca brahmaṇyaś cāvihiṃsakaḥ anasūyur apāpastho dvādaśāhaphalaṃ labhet
english: —free of greed, truthful, devoted to brāhmaṇas and harming none, without malice and standing clear of sin, he gains the fruit of the Dvādaśāha rite.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamayaṃ divyaṃ vimānaṃ haṃsalakṣaṇam sūryamālāsamābhāsam ārohet pāṇḍuraṃ gṛham
english: He mounts a divine celestial car wrought of pure gold, marked with the sign of the swan and gleaming like a wreath of suns—a pale and shining mansion.

sanskrit: āvartanāni catvāri tathā padmāni dvādaśa śarāgniparimāṇaṃ ca tatrāsau vasate sukham
english: There he dwells in bliss for four returns and twelve padmas, a span measured by the count of the arrows and the fires.

sanskrit: divase yas tu ṣaṣṭhe vai muniḥ prāśeta bhojanam sadā dvādaśamāsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: And the sage who eats his meal only on every sixth day, for all twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: sadā triṣavaṇasnāyī brahmacāry anasūyakaḥ gavāmayasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam
english: —ever bathing at the three appointed times, chaste, and free of malice, he gains the unsurpassed fruit of the Gavāmayana sacrifice.

sanskrit: agnijvālāsamābhāsaṃ haṃsabarhiṇasevitam śātakumbhamayaṃ yuktaṃ sādhayed yānam uttamam
english: He wins a supreme vehicle, fashioned of gold and yoked, bright as the flame of fire and attended by swans and peacocks.

sanskrit: tathaivāpsarasām aṅke prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate nūpurāṇāṃ ninādena mekhalānāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ
english: And asleep there in the lap of the apsarases, he is awakened by the chime of anklets and the jingling of girdles.

sanskrit: koṭīsahasraṃ varṣāṇāṃ trīṇi koṭiśatāni ca padmāny aṣṭādaśa tathā patāke dve tathaiva ca
english: A thousand koṭis of years, and three hundred koṭis besides, eighteen padmas, and likewise two patākas—

sanskrit: ayutāni ca pañcāśad ṛkṣacarmaśatasya ca lomnāṃ pramāṇena samaṃ brahmaloke mahīyate
english: —and fifty myriads more: by a span equal to the number of hairs on a hundred bear-skins, he is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: divase saptame yas tu prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśamāsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: And he who eats only on every seventh day a single meal, for all twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ gopayāno brahmacaryaṃ samācaran sumanovarṇakaṃ caiva madhumāṃsaṃ ca varjayet
english: —guarding his speech, practising chastity, and shunning flowers, fragrant unguents, honey, and meat—

sanskrit: puruṣo marutāṃ lokam indralokaṃ ca gacchati tatra tatra ca siddhārtho devakanyābhir uhyate
english: —such a man goes to the world of the Maruts and to the world of Indra, and there, his aim achieved, he is borne aloft by the daughters of the gods.

sanskrit: phalaṃ bahusuvarṇasya yajñasya labhate naraḥ saṃkhyām atiguṇāṃ cāpi teṣu lokeṣu modate
english: That man gains the fruit of the Bahusuvarṇa sacrifice, and rejoices in those worlds for a span beyond all reckoning.

sanskrit: yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ kṣānto bhuṅkte 'hany aṣṭame naraḥ devakāryaparo nityaṃ juhvāno jātavedasam
english: And the man who, patient through a whole year, eats only on every eighth day, ever intent upon the service of the gods and pouring oblations into Jātavedas the fire—

sanskrit: pauṇḍarīkasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam padmavarṇanibhaṃ caiva vimānam adhirohati
english: —gains the unsurpassed fruit of the Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice, and mounts a celestial car of the hue of the lotus.
